## About these materials

**Welcome!**

These materials focus on how to take action and address challenges within Open Science. Awareness of our own spheres of influence is an important step towards positive change. These materials, put into practice the skills learned about effective leadership using case studies that featuring challenges such as doing a preregistration and navigating large-scale collaborations. Equipped with a diverse set of strategies, Open Science leaders can then more confidently apply them to own research and teaching contexts.

The case study series on leadership in Open Science is co-developed by the LMU Open Science Center and the Framework for Open and Reproducible Research Training ([FORRT](https://forrt.org/)).

*Case studies:*

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
| Case study | Key themes | Where to find this |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Contributorship under tension | Authorship decision making, CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy), power dynamics | click [here](https://zenodo.org/records/22307117) to access |
| Paulo’s preregistration problem | Preregistration, supervisor-student relationship, self-advocacy | click [here](https://zenodo.org/records/22307709) to access |
| Alex’s open code dilemma | Generative AI, reproducible code | click [here](https://zenodo.org/records/22306455) to access |
| Finn’s struggle to choose a method(ology) | Qualitative research methods, academic rigor | click [here](https://zenodo.org/records/22308007) to access |
| Listening beyond the protocol: Roya’s experience with cultural ways of knowing | Qualitative research methods, research ethics | click [here](https://zenodo.org/records/22308238) to access |
:::

### Who are these materials for?

The target audience for these materials are twofold:

- **Aspiring Open Research Instructors** or **self-learners** with familiarity about key Open Research issues and challenges (e.g., reproducibility and replicability), Open Research tools (e.g., computational reproducibility, preregistration, study planning), basic didactic and lesson conceptualization skills who are interested in building didactic skills to effectively teach Open Research through a combination of theoretical input and practical exercises to become **Open Research Instructors**. You can follow these materials by chronologically going through the slides and following along with the practical exercises. You go at your own pace and within your own timeframe. *Presenter notes* will help you to understand and reflect on the content of the materials. Note: Group exercises are *not* possible in this asynchronous setting.

- **Future or current Open Research instructors** in higher education (e.g., universities, colleges) who are interested or already engaging in bringing Open Research topics closer to your learners and want to sharpen their own didactic skills for effective teaching; or instructors aiming to *train others* in delivering high-quality Open Research Education. The slides can be directly presented in full screen below, with presenter and instructor notes providing detailed information about the content of the materials and valuable pedagogical tips how to convey the materials to your learners. You can also download the PowerPoint or pdf file corresponding to the materials below and adapt the materials to your learners. Make sure to give appropriate credit to the original authors.

### Prerequisites

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
| Prerequisite | Description | Where to find this |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Basic familiarity with Open Science practices | Examples: R, preregistration, Open Access etc. | [Click here to get familiar with Open Science first](https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-student-track-OS/) |
| Knowledge of CRediT roles | CRediT - Contributor Roles Taxonomy | [Click here to get familiar with CRediT roles first](https://credit.niso.org/)) |
:::

### Learning objectives

- **Examine** approaches to addressing challenges in Open Science from multiple perspectives to increase breadth of knowledge.
- **Discuss** and **propose** actionable and equitable strategies to address challenges in Open Science as a way to relate to own leadership contexts and build up collective problem-solving skills.
